fatal_errors: The proposed Mg-Mn/Zr-Si composition and transient-liquid intervention replace the target ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo BCC alloy and SPS-at-1000 °C intervention.

At 850 °C, magnesium is already above its approximately 650 °C melting point, so describing Mg-Si as a minor transient liquid within an otherwise solid Mg matrix is physically misleading without a demonstrated constrained liquid-phase process.
The claimed Mg-Si eutectic behavior, >98% density, volatility thresholds, and suppression of transition-metal segregation are not supported by the cited evidence.
The hypothesis omits the target oxide barrier phases, 900 °C oxidation test, biphasic parabolic oxidation kinetics, and the reported optimum at 1000 °C.
The asserted volatility boundary above 920 °C conflicts with the target result showing successful SPS at 1000 °C.
explanation: The response addresses the general themes of Mg-containing lightweight alloys, densification, segregation, volatility, and barrier performance, and it proposes a reasonably falsifiable temperature/additive matrix with density, XRD/EDS, NaCl polarization, and mass-loss measurements. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target study: it changes the alloy system, additive strategy, optimum temperature, phases, mechanism, and predicted outcome. Its prior-evidence discipline is especially weak. E1 concerns oxidation of a different refractory high-entropy alloy, while E2 only supports the generic concept of protective oxide films; neither validates Mg-Si liquid-phase sintering or the numerical density and volatility boundaries. The central processing description is also questionable because Mg would be molten at 850 °C. Thus, although the experiment could discriminate the proposed alternative internally, the hypothesis is insufficiently supported and scientifically inconsistent with the hidden target.
